frequency_question: How often do nations establish operational domestic manufacturing lines for advanced imported guided weapons within 36 months of conflict onset?
membership_rule: Includes state-level programs attempting to shift from direct import of sophisticated cruise missiles or precision glide munitions to domestic assembly/manufacturing during active high-intensity conflict. Excludes simple licensed production initiated and completed entirely during peacetime.

cases.name: UK wartime domestic production of American Bofors/Oerlikon and aviation tech
Taiwan Hsiung Feng missile series domestic scaling
Iran reverse-engineering and domestic production of Hawk/Stinger/cruise missile variants under sanctions and war

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named cases representing the complete class of major wartime advanced missile/ordnance localization efforts under duress since WWII.
known_gaps: Modern software-heavy cruise missiles present vastly higher integration hurdles than 20th-century ordnance, representing a structural upward friction not fully captured by older historical analogues.
skeleton: 3 major historical precedents of urgent wartime defense industrial localization under external constraints, yielding 3 hits out of 3 relevant major state efforts where political will and external technical assistance aligned.
validity_reason: Industrial base resilience and modern supply chain globalization rates remain stable through the end of the decade.
